Posterior of the event rates under the exposure-time Poisson model

Source: R/exptime_post.R
exptime_post.Rd

Computes the posterior distribution of the event rates of study drug and control under the Bayesian exposure-time model of Schnell and Ball (2016) from blinded subject-level data: the number of events and the follow-up time of each subject.

Usage

exptime_post(
  y,
  t,
  k = 1,
  prior_c,
  prior_d,
  rate0 = NULL,
  rr0 = 1,
  cutoff = 0.95,
  level = 0.95,
  details = TRUE,
  control = list()
)

Arguments

y

Numbers of events of the subjects (non-negative integers).

t

Follow-up times of the subjects (positive), in the time unit of the rates.

k

Randomization ratio of study drug to control (k:1).

prior_c

Shape and rate c(alpha_c, beta_c) of the Gamma prior of the control rate.

prior_d

Shape and rate c(alpha_d, beta_d) of the Gamma prior of the study drug rate.

rate0

Optional critical value of the study drug rate.

rr0

Critical value of the rate ratio, used for the signal when rate0 is NULL.

cutoff

Posterior probability threshold for a signal.

level

Probability of the equal-tailed credible intervals.

details

Logical; if FALSE, the quantiles are not computed (they are NA). This is faster.

control

List of settings of the numerical integration: n_coarse (cells per coordinate of the coarse grid, default 41), n_u and n_v (nodes of the two coordinates, defaults 48 and 49), check (default TRUE), eps (default 1e-8) and max_iter (default 12).

Value

An object of class bssd_post, a list with elements

model

"EXPTIME".

prob

Posterior probability of the tested quantity (lambda_d > rate0, or r > rr0 when rate0 is NULL).

signal

Logical; prob > cutoff.

probs

Both posterior probabilities: drug (\(\lambda_d > rate_0\), NA without rate0) and ratio (\(r > rr_0\)).

rr

Posterior mean, median and the limits of the equal-tailed credible interval of the rate ratio \(r\).

rate

The same summaries of \(\lambda_d\).

estimates

Posterior means of lambda_c, lambda_d, r and the difference \(\lambda_d - \lambda_c\).

rr_label, rr0, rr_name, rate_name, description, cutoff, level

Labels and settings used by print.

data, prior

Data summary and prior parameters.

integration

Description of the numerical integration.

Details

For subject \(i\) with follow-up time \(t_i\) and \(y_i\) events, the model is $$Y_i \mid a_i \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda_{a_i} t_i), \quad a_i \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(k / (k + 1)),$$ $$\lambda_c \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(\alpha_c, \beta_c), \quad \lambda_d \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(\alpha_d, \beta_d),$$ where \(a_i = 1\) means study drug and the Gamma distributions are parameterized by shape and rate. Summing over the unknown treatment assignment of each subject gives the likelihood $$\prod_i [\lambda_c^{y_i} e^{-\lambda_c t_i} / (k + 1) + k \lambda_d^{y_i} e^{-\lambda_d t_i} / (k + 1)],$$ so the posterior is two-dimensional. Schnell and Ball (2016) sample it by Gibbs sampling; here it is integrated numerically on the coordinates \(\log \lambda_c\) (Gauss-Legendre quadrature) and the prior distribution function of \(\lambda_d\) (Chebyshev interpolation), after a coarse grid has located the region that holds all but control$eps of the posterior mass. When control$check is TRUE, the computation is repeated with about 1.5 times as many nodes, the finer result is returned, and the largest absolute difference in the posterior probabilities is reported as the integration error estimate.

The prior of the control rate is expected to be informative (for example, a posterior from historical control data); without it the blinded data do not separate the two rates.

When rate0 is given, a signal is declared when \(P(\lambda_d > rate_0 \mid \mathrm{data}) > \) cutoff, which is the rule of Schnell and Ball (2016); otherwise the rate ratio \(r = \lambda_d / \lambda_c\) is tested against rr0. Both probabilities are returned in probs.

With event indicators as y and the times at risk (follow-up up to the first event) as t, the model is the exponential model for the time to the first event.

References

Schnell, P. M. and Ball, G. (2016). A Bayesian exposure-time method for clinical trial safety monitoring with blinded data. Therapeutic Innovation & Regulatory Science, 50(6), 833–838. doi:10.1177/2168479016656702

See also

elicit_prior for priors from quantiles, expbern_post for the exponential Bernoulli mixture model.

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 300
t <- runif(n, 6, 18)
drug <- rbinom(n, 1, 2 / 3)
y <- rpois(n, ifelse(drug == 1, 0.016, 0.011) * t)
# priors of Schnell and Ball (2016): control rate from 339 events in 26064
# person-months, study drug rate with one hundredth of that information
fit <- exptime_post(y, t, k = 2, prior_c = c(339, 26064),
                    prior_d = c(339 / 100 + 4, 26064 / 100 + 167),
                    rate0 = 0.0156, cutoff = 0.62)
fit
#> Model: EXPTIME 
#> Tested quantity: event rate lambda_d of study drug
#> P(lambda_d > 0.0156 | data) = 0.5387
#> Signal (posterior probability > 0.62): no
#> Posterior of r: mean 1.234, median 1.221, 95% interval (0.8188, 1.721)
#> Posterior of lambda_d: mean 0.01599, median 0.01587, 95% interval (0.01092, 0.02176)
